extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions, Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal counsel, and other stakeholders participating in or affected by Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and discussion of the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations addressing the definition and scope of 'pregnancy or related conditions,' parental status, admissions protections, pre-admission inquiries, and related compliance obligations for recipients of federal education funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'termination of pregnancy' in 'pregnancy or related conditions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department includes “termination of pregnancy” within the definition of “pregnancy or related conditions” and rejects calls to wholly exempt abortion or abortion services from that definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies that recipients can implement these regulations without asking questions of a student, employee, or applicant about the specific circumstances surrounding the person's pregnancy or related conditions, including a potential or past abortion. Inquiries into the circumstances of an abortion may be discriminatory (for example, if informed by sex stereotypes or handled differently than other temporary medical conditions) or may impermissibly deter exercise of Title IX rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1688 does not mandate exempting abortion from coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Although section 1688 provides a partial limitation on the Department's ability to enforce section 1681’s nondiscrimination protection related to abortion, the Department disagrees that section 1688 requires it to wholly exempt abortion and abortion services from the proposed definition of “pregnancy or related conditions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1688 limits construing Title IX to require or prohibit provision or payment for abortion-related benefits or services, but it does not preclude including termination of pregnancy within the nondiscrimination protections of Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not discriminate based on termination of pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: A policy or action that specifically targets individuals who have received abortion care for adverse treatment may violate the general nondiscrimination mandate in section 1681.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates its longstanding interpretation that ensuring equal access for students or employees who seek or have had abortions is within Title IX obligations. Targeted adverse treatment of those who received abortion care can constitute unlawful sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for students (case-by-case, not required for employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: For students, recipients must make reasonable modifications as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity based on the student's individualized needs in consultation with the student; recipients are not required to provide reasonable modifications to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reasonable modifications will be determined on a case-by-case basis and the Department anticipates they typically will not be particularly expensive or extensive. See final §106.40(b)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space and related accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations contain provisions providing lactation space for students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes these provisions as part of protections aimed at enabling participation in education programs and activities without discrimination; these are separate from any requirement to provide or pay for abortion-related services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX does not require recipients to provide or pay for abortions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title IX or the final regulations requires recipients to provide or pay for any benefit or service, including the use of facilities, related to an abortion; the regulations abide by 20 U.S.C. 1688.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments asserting the regulations would require health insurance or health care to cover abortion misunderstand the text; Title IX obligations are limited to preventing discrimination and ensuring equal access rather than requiring funding of abortion services. Where programs also fall under Section 1557 or other laws, recipients must comply with those independent authorities as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy discrimination constitutes sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of pregnancy, including because of termination of pregnancy, is a form of sex discrimination (because pregnancy is a condition related to sex characteristics and because such discrimination often rests on sex stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites case law recognizing pregnancy discrimination as sex discrimination and gives examples (e.g., a professor excluding a student from field work based on a stereotype about recent termination of pregnancy). The Title IX regulations have historically considered termination of pregnancy an aspect of pregnancy discrimination since 1975.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment and religious freedom preserved; religious exemptions remain
rubrics_metrics.description: The pregnancy-related provisions do not limit §106.6(d) and do not restrict rights protected by the First Amendment or other constitutional guarantees; Title IX contains a statutory exemption for recipients controlled by religious organizations for provisions that conflict with specific tenets of the religious organization (20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3)), and §106.12 remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reaffirms that recipients cannot use Title IX to limit free exercise of religion or protected speech, and it directs readers to additional discussion of religious exemptions elsewhere in the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'parental status'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department defines “parental status” in §106.2 to include categories such as in loco parentis, legal custodian or guardian, and persons actively seeking legal custody, guardianship, visitation, or adoption; the definition does not bestow parental authority or alter state-determined parental rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is intended to clarify the scope of Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination related to parental status. The Department declines to list specific examples of who qualifies as 'in loco parentis' or legal guardian because such determinations depend on facts and state law. The Department also declined requests to raise the age of care recipients to 21 and declined to create a separate 'family status' definition, considering 'family status' sufficiently well understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions protections re parental, family, marital status and pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.21 prohibits recipients covered by Subpart C from discriminating against applicants based on current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions and prohibits implementing policies, practices, or procedures concerning parental, family, or marital status that treat applicants differently based on sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department made editorial changes for clarity in §106.21(c)(2) (e.g., replacing 'apply' with 'implement' and 'establish or follow' with 'adopt or implement'). The Department emphasizes ensuring an inclusive environment and that such protections help ensure equal access for applicants who are pregnant or parenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain pre-admission inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient covered by Subpart C must not make a pre-admission inquiry into the marital status of an applicant (final §106.21(c)(2)(iii)); more broadly, pre-admission inquiries or policies concerning parental, family, or marital status may not treat applicants differently based on sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add explicit language to §106.21(c)(2)(iii) to list 'current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions' or 'family status and parental status' because other provisions of the section already prohibit discrimination based on those statuses. The Department recognizes privacy and research implications (e.g., Common Application question about children) but holds that asking a question is permissible only if asked of all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart C (admissions) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart C of the regulations, which governs admissions, does not apply to nonvocational elementary and secondary schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 34 CFR 106.15(c),(d). Nonvocational elementary and secondary schools remain subject to §106.34(a) (general participation prohibitions) and §106.34(c) (single-sex admissions for public nonvocational elementary and secondary schools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declination to add 'perceived' and 'expected' labels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines requests to add the terms 'perceived' and 'expected' to the list of protected statuses in §106.21(c)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rationale is consistent with the Department's discussion of similar requests for the definition of pregnancy in §106.2 and further explained in the discussion of §106.10; the Department concluded the existing text already covers the relevant protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections for personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(j) prohibits the disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with the part, with some exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(j) in response to commenter concerns about maintaining confidentiality of PII when implementing the regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to help recipients respond to questions about the interaction of the final regulations with Title IX, Dobbs, and State laws restricting access to abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an implementation support commitment rather than a new legal requirement; it is intended to help recipients understand and comply with Title IX obligations in the context of state law restrictions.
